name: Churchill Island
bio_draft: 57-hectare island reached by causeway, with a heritage farm and a farmers' market.

facts.claim: Churchill Island Heritage Farm sits off Phillip Island with historic grounds, daily farming activities and bay walking trails.
Walking and cycling trails are free to enjoy; the site has bird-watching huts and a cafe.
Highland cattle experience and wagon rides (weekends and holidays) are extras on top of entry.

access_note: Adult entry $17.50 from the Nature Parks page; the $80 Bandicoot Discovery Tour and $60 Highland Cattle Experience are separate extras. Farmers' market is a periodic event, not a spot.

name: Cape Woolamai
bio_draft: cape with walking loops among shearwater burrows and a surf beach at the island's south-east.

facts.claim: Cape Woolamai is Phillip Island's highest point, with views over a surf beach and walking tracks along wind- and wave-carved cliffs.
Walks range from 4 to 8 km, including a Pinnacles return reached from the beach.
Short-tailed shearwaters arrive here in late September after migrating from the Aleutian Islands; walks may be impassable on very high tides.

access_note: Dogs not permitted; exposed, some bushwalking experience recommended.
unresolved: No fee mentioned on the Nature Parks page; treated as free open reserve

name: Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit
bio_draft: purpose-built 1950s circuit hosting the MotoGP Australian Grand Prix, open to visitors on non-event days through track tours.

facts.claim: The circuit hosts the world-leading motorsport series, including the WorldSBK round in February.
Circuit Viewing from the Visitor Centre water-gardens mound shows up to 80% of the track, including Stoner Corner and Siberia.
Circuit Viewing admission includes the History of Motorsport Display covering the island's racing since 1928.

access_note: Circuit Viewing availability is subject to circuit hire and seasonality; no track tours found on the site, so the draft bio's 'track tours' is unsupported. Event days cost more.

name: National Vietnam Veterans Museum
bio_draft: volunteer-run museum of Vietnam War memorabilia at Cape Woolamai, with over 5,000 items.

facts.claim: Museum on Australia's involvement in the Vietnam War with multiple galleries on the war and the experiences of Australian veterans.
Has a gift shop, the Nui Dat Cafe and a Garden of Reflection.
Located at 25 Veterans Drive, Newhaven.

access_note: Draft bio says Cape Woolamai; official address is Veterans Drive, Newhaven. '5,000 items' not confirmed.

name: Rhyll Inlet and Conservation Hill
bio_draft: inlet and wetlands at Rhyll, a feeding and breeding area for birds, with a boardwalk pathway.

facts.claim: Mangrove and mudflat wetlands on the north shore of Phillip Island, part of the Western Port Ramsar-listed wetland.
Boardwalks loop through mangroves and saltmarsh; spoonbills, oystercatchers, herons and migratory shorebirds feed here.
A 500 m return lookout walk climbs the Conservation Hill Observation Tower for views over the inlet and Western Port.
Mangrove boardwalk is 1.2 km return, about 45 minutes; trails start from the Conservation Hill car park on McIlwraith Rd.

unresolved: No fee mentioned; treated as free open reserve

name: Phillip Island Chocolate Factory
bio_draft: commercial factory with a paid interactive chocolate attraction (Panny's Amazing World of Chocolate) at Newhaven.

facts.claim: Retail shop and cafe have free entry; the ticketed Panny's Amazing World of Chocolate is an interactive factory tour with a chocolate waterfall.
Over 100 chocolate varieties are made on site.
Located at 930 Phillip Island Rd, Newhaven.

access_note: Adult (16+) $25.00 for the Panny's attraction; a second $18.00 adult tier was listed on the tickets page (likely a different package), so $25 is the standard.

name: A Maze'N Things
bio_draft: maze, mini-golf, illusions hall and adventure ropes course at Phillip Island Road.

facts.claim: Family park on Phillip Island with a giant 3D maze, Puzzle Island, Magic Manor illusions, a 19-hole mini golf course and the SkyTrail high ropes course
SkyTrail is a 10 m high ropes course with 30 obstacles
Indoor and outdoor attractions, so it runs in any weather; children up to 3 enter free

name: French Island
bio_draft: Western Port island with national park, koalas and waterbirds, reached by passenger ferry from Stony Point or Cowes.

facts.claim: French Island National Park covers heathland and open woodland and holds Victoria's most significant koala population
More than 230 bird species recorded, plus the long-nosed potoroo and released eastern barred bandicoots
Reached by Western Port Ferries passenger ferry from Stony Point (10-12 minutes to Tankerton Jetty) or from Cowes
Fairhaven Campground is a 5 km walk or ride from Tankerton Jetty

access_note: Ferry services can be cancelled at short notice; page shows a generic 'This area is closed' banner label, not verified as an actual closure

name: State Coal Mine
bio_draft: former coal mine museum at Wonthaggi, run by Parks Victoria, with underground tours.

facts.claim: Former state-owned black coal mine at Wonthaggi, operational 1910 to 1968, now a Parks Victoria heritage attraction
Guided underground tours (60-90 minutes) run daily at 11.30am and 2.00pm; children must be 5 or older
Entry to the aboveground attractions, visitor centre film and heritage trail is free
The drift car that carried visitors out of the mine has been suspended since 2020; walking tours resumed in 2024

name: Meeting of the Waters
bio_draft: Riverside park viewpoint at Wentworth where the Murray and Darling rivers meet, about 20 km west of Mildura.

facts.claim: Junction Park in Wentworth, NSW, is where the Darling River meets the Murray, the two longest rivers in Australia; it includes a lookout
Wentworth lies at the confluence of the Darling and Murray rivers, about 20 km west of Mildura
The Wentworth Trail passes heritage buildings and landmarks near the park, starting at the visitor information centre

name: Australian Inland Botanic Gardens
bio_draft: Semi-arid botanic gardens at Buronga, near Mildura, with plants from every inhabited continent and native species.

facts.claim: Community-created botanic garden at Buronga, NSW, billed as the Southern Hemisphere's first semi-arid botanic garden
Plantings showcase Australian arid and exotic flora, including a rose garden of over 1,600 bushes
Entrance is free, gold coin donation welcome

name: Apex Park
bio_draft: Riverside park on the Murray at Mildura with a sandbar swimming beach, sometimes patrolled.

facts.claim: Riverside park on the Murray in Mildura with a large sandbar beach good for swimming
Described as possibly Victoria's largest inland beach; occasionally patrolled by lifeguards

unresolved: lifeguard patrol seasons not verified

name: Port of Echuca
bio_draft: Historic 1800s river port with its wharf, paddle steamer boarding and the Discovery Centre at Echuca.

facts.claim: Living monument to the 1870s, when Echuca was the third largest port in Australia outside Sydney and Melbourne
Paddlesteamers depart daily from the Echuca Wharf, which originally ran 332 m in the 1880s
Discovery Centre has audiovisual displays on the inland river system, a working Evans Brothers sawmill and a steam display; PS Adelaide (built 1866) is moored at the wharf
Daily guided walking tours run twice a day; filming location of TV series All the Rivers Run

access_note: Entry to Discovery Centre and wharf reported free (local news report); tours and cruises are paid, prices not shown on the page (booking widget).
unresolved: Free entry is from a secondary news report; official page shows no entry price. Tour/cruise price not verified.

name: Barmah National Park
bio_draft: River red gum forest on the Murray floodplain with Barmah Lakes, birdwatching, paddling, fishing and camping.

facts.claim: Park on Yorta Yorta Country on the Murray floodplain, with walking trails through forest and along waterways and the Murray River
Oven mounds used for cooking by Traditional Owners can be seen along the Lakes Loop Track and Broken Creek Loop Track
Offers canoeing, birdwatching and camping

access_note: Parks Victoria page flags reported issues / closure notices (e.g. Sand Ridge track flooding); check before travel.

name: Dharnya Centre
bio_draft: Yorta Yorta cultural and environmental interpretation centre inside Barmah National Park.

facts.claim: Cultural hub of the Yorta Yorta people, inside Barmah National Park on Sand Ridge Track
Three walking trails start from the centre, including the 1.2 km Yamyabuc Trail loop with 13 interpretive markers on Yorta Yorta knowledge
Kingfisher river cruises on the Murray with an Aboriginal cultural focus; guided Yamyabuc walks led by a Yorta Yorta Knowledge Holder run on select days

access_note: Centre is being renewed with new facilities (2026); self-guided trails are free, the $65 adult price is the Kingfisher cruise. Parks Victoria site page flagged closed/issues notice. Verify.

name: Kyabram Fauna Park
bio_draft: Goulburn Valley wildlife park at Kyabram with native animals.

facts.claim: Zoos Victoria wildlife park at Kyabram in the Goulburn Valley
55 hectares of bushland and wetlands with more than 400 native animals including koalas, dingoes, kangaroos, wombats, emus and a meerkat exhibit
Daily keeper talks, animal encounters, walking trails and a water play park

access_note: Adult 'from $32' on the booking page; price may vary by day.

name: Terrick Terrick National Park
bio_draft: Small box-ironbark park near Pyramid Hill, with walking tracks and camping.

facts.claim: Park with granite outcrops, woodlands and endangered grasslands, popular with birdwatchers
Short, steep Grade 3 walk from the picnic area to the summit of Mt Terrick Terrick, with views over the park and farmland
Contains Victoria's most significant stand of White Cypress Pines, near Bennetts Rock

name: Murray-Sunset National Park
bio_draft: Victoria's largest national park, remote mallee country for 4WD, birdwatching, camping and stargazing.

facts.claim: Remote mallee park in Victoria's north-west with many bush camping areas
Activities listed include 4WD, birdwatching, canoeing and kayaking, hiking and cycling

access_note: Remote; many tracks 4WD only. Check Parks Victoria closures.
unresolved: Largest-in-Victoria claim not on fetched page; no entry fee line found (rule: Victorian national parks free).

name: Pink Lakes
bio_draft: Pink-hued salt lakes inside Murray-Sunset National Park, a favourite with photographers.

facts.claim: Salt lakes in Murray-Sunset National Park that turn pink in late summer from beta-carotene produced by the alga Dunaliella salina
The area was the site of a major salt industry from 1916 to 1975
Lake Becking campground is within the park

access_note: Parks Victoria page flags reported issues/closures in parts of Murray-Sunset; check before going. Park, not a gated attraction.

name: Hattah-Kulkyne National Park
bio_draft: Chain of Murray lakes, river red gums and bush tracks with camping, near Mildura.

facts.claim: National park near Mildura on the Murray River with a chain of lakes, visitor centre, Lake Mournpall Walk and Warepil Lookout Tower
Several camping areas including Lake Hattah and Lake Mournpall

access_note: Parks Victoria: environmental works (Victorian Murray Floodplain Restoration Project) from June to December 2026 bring heavy vehicles and temporary track closures in the northern park.

name: Wyperfeld National Park
bio_draft: Victoria's first national park, mallee bushland with walks and camping, reached from Hopetoun.

facts.claim: Semi-arid national park in Victoria's north-west with a chain of lake beds linked by Outlet Creek, the northern extension of the Wimmera River
Reached via Hopetoun on the Henty Highway; sealed road from Rainbow or Hopetoun to Wonga Camping area
Co-managed with Wotjobaluk Traditional Owners (Barengi Gadjin Land Council)

name: Lake Tyrrell
bio_draft: Intermittent salt lake near Sea Lake with a mirror-like surface that draws photographers.

facts.claim: Victoria's largest salt lake, about 20,860 ha, 6 km north of Sea Lake and 314 km north-west of Melbourne
Usually covered by about 5 cm of water in winter; in dry periods people can walk onto the salt crust

name: Gunbower National Park
bio_draft: River red gum forest on the Murray with bend camping areas for four wheel driving and camping.

facts.claim: 9,330 ha national park beside the Murray River between Echuca and Koondrook, about 250 km north of Melbourne
Many bend camping areas along the river; four wheel driving is a listed activity

access_note: Parks Victoria: recent rainfall and environmental watering are affecting access; some track closures in Gunbower State Forest.

name: Pioneer Settlement
bio_draft: Living history museum of 1850s cottages, horse-drawn carriages and a river cruise on the Murray at Swan Hill.

facts.claim: Open-air museum in Swan Hill that opened in 1966
Paddle steamer Gem runs the one-hour Pyap River Cruise
Evening laser light shows, Heartbeat of the Murray and Legends of the Mallee, run on set nights
